subsystems.name: Light source
subsystems.role: supplies the laser light that carries the data through the chip.

subsystems.name: Input encoding
subsystems.role: converts electronic data into the phase and amplitude of light.

subsystems.name: Matrix multiplier
subsystems.role: does the core multiply-accumulate in the optical domain.
parts: mesh of Mach-Zehnder interferometers, or banks of microring resonators

subsystems.name: Detection and accumulation
subsystems.role: turns the resulting light levels back into electrical signals.

subsystems.name: Nonlinearity and control
subsystems.role: applies the activation function and keeps the device stable.
parts: electronic activation stages, or nonlinear optical material

subsystems.name: Packaging
subsystems.role: gets light in and out without losing it.

buildSteps.title: Map the network onto optics
buildSteps.detail: Train the model in software, then factor each weight matrix into a sequence of phase shifts and beam splitters that a photonic circuit can implement.

buildSteps.title: Design the circuit
buildSteps.detail: Lay out waveguides, interferometer meshes or ring banks on a photonic chip, respecting bend radii, crossings and loss budgets; free-space designs instead compute a stack of phase masks.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the chip
buildSteps.detail: Pattern silicon-on-insulator wafers with deep-ultraviolet lithography and etch the waveguides — the same tooling used for CMOS electronics. Diffractive designs are instead printed or lithographically etched as thin phase plates.

buildSteps.title: Add active elements
buildSteps.detail: Dope regions to make modulators and photodiodes; deposit heaters or electro-optic materials for tunable phase shifters.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the laser and detectors
buildSteps.detail: Bond or couple laser sources and attach photodetectors, since silicon itself does not emit light efficiently.

buildSteps.title: Package and align
buildSteps.detail: Align fibre arrays to sub-micron tolerance, glue, and mount the chip on a temperature-stabilised board.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the weights
buildSteps.detail: Measure the output for known inputs, then set each phase shifter until the mesh reproduces the trained matrix; repeat as temperature drifts.

buildSteps.title: Run and correct
buildSteps.detail: Feed data in, read results out, and use electronic stages to add nonlinearity and to compensate for the analogue errors, crosstalk and drift that pure optics cannot avoid.

prerequisites.why: CMOS-compatible foundries can now make thousands of optical components on one chip.
weights must be written into the circuit as phase or amplitude settings.
applying activation functions purely with light needs materials and power levels that are not yet practical, so most systems convert back to electronics between layers.
waveguide loss, modulator drive power, laser power and thermal tuning all eat into the energy advantage optics is supposed to deliver.
analogue hardware drifts with temperature, and re-training must compensate for manufacturing variation.

pathway.milestone: laboratory and small commercial demonstrations performing matrix multiplies with light, usually hybrid optical-electronic and limited in matrix size and depth
pathway.unlocks: evidence that photonic multiply-accumulate can work at useful speed and low latency.

pathway.milestone: co-packaged optics for data-centre links inside and between AI accelerator clusters
pathway.unlocks: volume photonic manufacturing, which the more ambitious neural-network chips depend on.

pathway.milestone: photonic accelerator cards handling the linear layers of inference models alongside conventional GPUs
pathway.unlocks: measurable energy and latency savings on real workloads, or a clear verdict that they are not there.

pathway.milestone: optical nonlinear elements and in-memory photonic weights, allowing many layers to stay in the light domain
pathway.unlocks: a genuine departure from electronic AI hardware rather than an accelerator bolted onto it.
